title: Fertilizer intensity feasibility investigation
question: Does district-level fertilizer application intensity account for statistical variation in the remaining cross-regional agricultural gap between Andhra Pradesh/Telangana and Tamil Nadu?
status: NOT FEASIBLE WITH CURRENT VERIFIED SOURCES

boundary_compatibility.reason: Single-year cross-section; both regions measured on 2011-12 boundaries
boundary_compatibility.coimbatore_erode: Measured on post-2009 boundaries in both the fertilizer and denominator tables, therefore internally consistent for this year (unlike the Experiment 6 irrigation panel, where they were BOUNDARY_NOT_COMPARABLE across years)

leakage_risks.basis: Fertilizer tonnage contains no yield component
Net area sown (all crops) is not rice area
One observed year makes the variable static per district, i.e. a district identifier. Same failure mode as soil (Exp 1), n_rice_seasons (Exp 4), single-year irrigation (Exp 5)
Two publications, two agencies, two terms, no definitions. Any systematic AP-vs-TN reporting difference loads directly and entirely onto the is_tn contrast
Broadcasting a 2011-12 observation across the 2000-2012 panel makes ~90% of rows anachronistic, against 31% in Experiment 5
Fertilizer supply responds to past and expected production; a single cross-section offers no identification strategy

primary_reasons: The definitional mismatch between AP 'distribution' and TN 'consumption' is unresolved and is confounded with the AP/TN contrast being measured.
Only one matched year exists, so the within-district differenced design that neutralised this class of confound in Experiment 6 is impossible.
Broadcasting 2011-12 values across the 2000-2012 panel would create severe temporal leakage and is prohibited.
Restricting to Kharif 2011 leaves a single-year cross-section of N approx 31 with a static district-level regressor and high district-fingerprinting risk.
Intensity normalization solves district-size scaling but does not address definition comparability or single-year identification.
conclusions.analogy: Reproduces the n_rice_seasons failure mode from Experiment 4 (reporting convention masquerading as agronomy), except undetectable here because it is confounded with region by construction. No robustness test available at N approx 31 could separate the two.
does_not_claim: That fertilizer has no effect on yield
would_change_verdict: An official methodology statement establishing a shared measurement basis (GoI DES route unreachable but not exhausted; FAI Fertiliser Statistics is the other candidate)
A second observed year for BOTH regions (TN District Statistical Handbooks unexplored; AP/TG is the binding constraint)
Reframing to a within-region question, though the single-year constraint forecloses this too
conclusions.further_search_note: Any additional fertilizer source discovery must be commissioned as a separate, explicitly approved task, and any resulting experiment treated as a new experiment.
